check_events.who: reader_b, GPT-6 Astra Pro, inherited, run SP85_C13_149
check_events.outcome: For a continuous homomorphism f:H→G of profinite groups, the image J is compact and hence closed in the Hausdorff group G. If J is open, its open cosets cover compact G, so finitely many cosets suffice and [G:J] is finite. Conversely, if [G:J] is finite, the complement of the closed subgroup J is a finite union of closed cosets and is closed; hence J is open. Thus the page's open-image condition is equivalent to finite-index image in this setting. This auxiliary topological check does not prove the proposed anabelian reconstruction correspondence or the classification question.

check_events.outcome: For a continuous homomorphism H to G of profinite groups the image is compact, hence closed because G is Hausdorff. If the image is open, compactness of G gives a finite subcover of its open cosets, hence finite index. If its index is finite, all other cosets are closed and their finite union is the closed complement, hence the image is open. Root used and rechecked exactly this auxiliary equivalence; no reconstruction claim is verified.
